correctness.rationale: For T=(B,D;0,0), T=TUT in the restricted semigroup implies im T⊆T(W), and a right inverse of B on im B extended linearly to W gives the converse. Equivalently V=W+ker T, so one can choose a complement to W inside ker T. This gives a W-preserving normal form B⊕0, and any W-preserving conjugacy must preserve the similarity class of the restriction. Thus the orbits are exactly indexed by partitions λ of r, with ambient type λ∪(1^c), rank r−ℓ(λ), and index λ_1. The column choices give q^(c(r−ℓ(λ))) lifts per B. The Jordan-module endomorphism algebra has dimension Σ(λ'_j)^2; invertibility on the module is equivalent to invertibility of each size-diagonal block modulo t, giving the stated centralizer factors. For an independent derivation of the total, write a_k for the number of nilpotent k×k matrices. The unique Fitting decomposition of an arbitrary r×r endomorphism gives q^(r²)/|GL_r|=Σ_(k=0)^r a_k/|GL_k| by counting complementary subspaces and choices on the two summands. Taking the consecutive difference gives a_r=q^(r²−r). Arbitrary columns are allowed for all nilpotent lifts, while only λ=(r) gives exponent q^(−c) in the regular fraction; the others are O_(r,q)(q^(−2c)). The r=1 identity and c=0 case agree with the formulas. For c>0 a single maximal chain in W can be extended by one complementary vector iff its image is chosen outside im B; this proves the unrestricted maximum r+1 versus regular maximum r. Independent finite enumeration reproduced 13/64 and 211/512 and confirmed the inner-inverse test for all 64 maps at (q,r,c)=(2,2,1).
residual_risks: The enumerations are checks in small prime fields only. It is the field-independent linear argument and finite-field cardinality calculation that cover arbitrary prime powers.

evidence: Sullivan explicitly characterizes regular elements by Vα⊆Wα. Grau gives the corresponding criterion Aα⊆Bα in an independence algebra.

With the quotient V/W having zero action, regularity is equivalent to splitting off V/W as trivial modules: W+ker T=V. Conjugacy of a pair (T,W) in this split class is equivalent to ordinary similarity on W, but the conjugacy orbit cardinality in the space of restricted-range matrices is not the ordinary GL(W) orbit cardinality.

Green's classes classify a different equivalence relation; the extra q-power counts distinct embeddings of a lift at fixed restriction, not a new Jordan centralizer.

value.rationale: Within the natural regular stratum of a restricted-range linear semigroup, the relative conjugacy problem, exact partition counts and rank/index distribution answer a complete structural question. In particular the formulas quantify how adding directions outside W makes regularity exponentially rare among nilpotents even though the possible nonregular index increases by one. These are useful all-parameter statistics of the constrained model, not arbitrary examples, and the proof identifies why ordinary similarity suffices despite using the smaller stabilizer group.
residual_risks: The finite-field result neither classifies nonregular parabolic orbits nor extends the enumeration to arbitrary independence algebras.
